question: A neutral, solid conducting sphere of radius $2R$ contains an off-center spherical cavity of radius $R/2$. The center of the cavity is located at a distance $R$ from the center of the large sphere. A point charge $+q$ is placed at the exact center of the cavity. What is the electric potential at the center of the large conducting sphere?

options.D: Zero, because the conductor is electrically neutral.
